preview: Interview experience of Smit Sekhadia at Hilti for an internship role in 2022, detailing the online assessment, technical interview, HR round, and preparation resources.
content: HTSI Interview Experience Smit Sekhadia Third Year Information Technology Location: Pune Stipend: 80,000 INR. Unlike the previous year, Hilti had come before the mid-term exams. The online assessment was on 1st Sept at 6pm. (an hour after the PPT) The test had 61 questions in total, the segregation was: 1 coding question (DSA) 30 Aptitude MCQs Rest of the questions were from OOPs, OS, DBMS, CN and DSA (6-7 questions each and were MCQs) The test was for 90 mins in total. The test was on mettl and we had to allow camera and microphone access. 1) ONLINE TEST Coding Section: We were given an array = [1 4 5 4 5] We had to change the elements that were repeated to the next minimum element such that the sum of all the elements is minimum and greater than the original sum. We had to return the new sum of the modified array. In the above example the modified array will be [1 4 5 6 7] and the ans will be 23 (1+4+5+6+7) which is the minimum sum and greater than the original sum (19). I solved it using Greedy approach and was able to pass all the testcases successfully. Aptitude Section (30 questions in 30 mins) All the questions in this section were easy but the challenge here was the time constraint. This section was also pretty good. MCQ Section The remaining time was given for the mcq section for DSA, DBMS, OOPs, OS and CN. Due to the time constraint i was not able to solve all the questions of DBMS and CN but i did well in DSA, OS and OOPs. There was no negative marking. The questions in this section were pretty good and needed clear fundamentals of the subjects. The result was out within an hour after the completion of the Online Assessment. Total 250+ students took the online test out of which 26 students were shortlisted for the interviews which were on the very next day. 2) INTERVIEW ROUND Date: 2nd Sept 22 A night before the interviews, the shortlisted students were asked to submit their resumes on a drive link. Technical Interview 1 The interview took place on Microsoft teams. My interview was scheduled for 3:45pm but I got the message to join the link at 3:25pm (if the interviews are online be ready at least half an hour before the interview.) I was admitted into the room after 5 mins. The HR greeted me and congratulated me for clearing the online assessment and wished me best of luck for the interview process. I was assigned to a breakout room after 2 mins. There was a single interviewer and she was very friendly. She asked me how my day was, was i nervous for the interview and told me to calm down. She told me that i should call her by her name and not ma'am as that's the culture they follow at hilti. (Treating everyone as equals) First she introduced herself and then asked me for my introduction whenever I was comfortable to start. Be prepared for your introduction as all the interviewers will ask you to introduce yourself first. Always mention any one of your projects in your introduction which you had worked on and the major achievements that you have achieved. Also mention your hobbies and what you do in your free time. In the introduction i told her about the project i had developed about Smart India Hackathon that last week me and my team had went to tamil nadu for the hackathon.after my introduction she was interested in the project and asked me to describe it more. Try to follow the STAR (Situation, Task, Action, Result). I explained to her the project (The Problem Statement, how our project manage to solve the problem, what work i had done in the project, always say the things that u have done in the project if its a team project) and she was quite interested in it and asked what techstack we had used for the project. I said for the frontend we had used NextJS and it was the first time I had worked with NextJS.The database that we used was postgreSQL with GraphQL. She showed more interest in the project and we continued the discussion on the project. Then she moved on and asked me which language I was proficient in. I said c++ and that I had done DSA and OOPs in c++. Then she asked me which languages were in my curriculum throughout the semesters.I said we had C++ in sem2 and DSA in java in sem3. Then she asked me what is the difference between method overriding and method overloading. I was able to answer this correctly and she was satisfied.Then she asked me whether we have a destructor in java? I said there is no destructor in java. She continued to ask me What destroys the object in java? I answered the garbage collector and she was satisfied. She asked me what are other roles of garbage collector? I was able to answer this correctly. She then asked me how the object gets destroyed in c++? And if no destructor is specified then is there a default destructor invoked? She tried to confuse me here but later I got it right. I was able to answer all these questions correctly and she was satisfied with my answers. She then moved on and asked which data structures I had worked with? I named quite a few data structures in which I was confident she then asked me what is the difference between a regular linked list and circular linked list. She was satisfied with my answer. She then asked me do you know recursion and to explain it. I explained to her properly, also stating different types of recursion (head recursion,tail recursion ,nested recursion etc). She then asked me to write any code of recursion and to explain it to her. She was convinced with my code and explanation. Moving on with DBMS, she asked me if we had dbms in our curriculum and what all we had covered. I said we had covered all the keys, referential integrity constraints, queries in sql, normalisation, transaction protocols etc. She asked me whether I have used any database in my projects, I said I had worked with postgreSQL in ReachOut and explained to her the schema for the table was constructed in supabase and queries were generated using GraphQL. She asked me why I had used postgreSQL for the project and why not a NoSQL database (This is the most common question asked when you use a SQL database in a project so I was well prepared for the same). She asked me whether I had any questions. I asked what projects do the interns get to work on? She gave a brief answer and I asked some follow up questions on the techstack too. At the end she said “I'll recommend you for the HR round, don't worry about that”. I was shocked for a second as the interviewers don't usually say that you will proceed for the next round. This round lasted 43 mins. I was happy that it ended on a good note.She was very friendly and did not make it feel like an actual company interview rather it was more like a discussion. 15 students were selected for the HR round. I received the message at 4:38pm to be ready for the HR round. I was told to join the link at 5:00pm. HR Interview I was again greeted by the HR and he congratulated me on getting selected for the HR round and asked me how my technical round was. This round was more like a friendly conversation. He asked me to introduce myself (Here don't say too much about your projects and coding skills as they are here to judge you on your personality and not your coding skills) i gave a brief introduction about myself.he then asked me where i was born, told me to tell more about my family background and schooling. I answered all the questions (make sure you answer all the questions in the same sequence they are asked, else you might forget what the first question was). He then asked me why have you applied to Hilti? I gave him several reasons and he was quite happy with my answer. He asked me what qualities do i have that we should hire you? These types of questions always state a quality and give a real life example to justify it (please dont lie here as they will get to know about it eventually). He asked me how will you convince your mom and dad that you are joining a company who for many years has been in the construction business? I answered this question confidently as i already knew in the prev round the interviewer had told me the projects and techstacks that the intern gets to work on. He asked me, among the shortlisted candidates, who do you think is most deserving? I named a friend who had genuinely worked hard. He then asked me while laughing, between you and him, who should we select? I also started laughing when he said no need to answer that question and that he was just messing around. He then asked me which domain I was interested in for the internship. I said I am looking forward to learning new things, so any project on the software part would be fine. He then asked me what if we don't give you a software project but appoint you for the QA? I said i am looking for real world corporate experience and as long as i am getting that any role is fine.i just need company exposure for my professional life and that I thought hilti is the right company for it. He was quite happy with my answer and smiled. He asked me whether I had any questions? I asked which real world projects has he been exposed to? He gave a detailed answer explaining various projects he had worked on in the past years. In conclusion he said to me we have several smart students to select from, and we might not always take the best call but all the best for the result. This statement got me thinking what I had said wrong throughout the interview. After the interview I was thinking that I wouldn't be selected. The round lasted for 30 mins. At 7:00 pm results were announced, selecting 7 students and luckily I was one of them. Maybe the last suggestion was related to all the students in general rather than me. 3) The Preparation 1) For DSA I followed DSA450 sheet by Love Babbar and Leetcode problems. 2) You can refer to the notes and code written by me on github 3) Be sure to cover the following topics: Arrays, Strings, Linked List, Sliding Window (IMP), Stacks and Queues. 4) Refer to the Aditya Verma playlist on Youtube for Dynamic Programming, Sliding Window, and Stacks. 5) I referred GateSmashers playlist for Operating Systems. 6) I followed cheat sheets of Love Babbar for OS, DBMS, and OOPs 7) For SQL queries I referred Top 30 SQL Queries by Edureka, and practise queries on leetcode as well. 8) I used to see mock interviews on youtube whenever I was free, that helped me quite a lot about how to answer in the interviews and to think out loudly so the interviewer knows how you are approaching the problem. 9) Don't loose faith in yourself if you get rejected, i was rejected in DE Shaw interviews and SAP Labs interviews.Make note of the things that went wrong in these interviews and learn from those mistakes These are experiences which will help you in the interviews you will be giving. 10) Lastly, TRUST your preparation and fod ke aao :)
